pairs.evidence: app/features/tools/devcases/DevLifecycleReviewPanel.tsx:186 The approval drawer puts the structural probe-strength verdict next to the internal-only probe list before a human signs off, and the workspace types record mid-flight, decision-log and follow-up evidence as observations, with an explicit not-measured state.

techniques.evidence: app/features/tools/devcases/DevLifecycleReviewPanel.tsx:186 The reviewer sees the probe audit before approving. The 422 probe_audit_failed refusal is localised and names the regenerate exit (line 41). The UI never sends overrideProbeAudit, so a 'none' case cannot be shipped from this surface at all.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevLifecycleReviewPanel.tsx:175 Probes render as an internal, locked panel. The candidate-safe preview leaves them out by construction (lines 69-70). DevTypes.ts:475-481 keeps 'detected, not graded' from showing as 'missed', so an unmeasured probe is not counted as a failure.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevTypes.ts:294 Follow-ups are minted per candidate and tied to the decision the candidate visibly made. listenFor/redFlag stay interviewer-internal (DevShared.tsx:142). Only the data shape is judged here; the question forms are written in the pipeline, outside this context.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevTypes.ts:301 Whether a DECISIONS log exists is telemetry, not a score, and an unreadable tree is null/unknown rather than 'missing' (line 306). How the log is framed to the candidate lives in the seed materializer, outside this context, so it is not judged here.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevTypes.ts:260 What the candidate did after the perturbation is a first-class observation, and 'never shown' renders as no signal rather than zero adaptation. The perturbation itself is injected outside this context.

pairs.evidence: app/api/devcase/lifecycle/[id]/approve/route.ts:132 A 'none'-verdict override is written to the audit trail with only the actor class 'human' and no principal, so the record cannot say who chose to ship a known-blind instrument, which the technique requires of every override.

techniques.evidence: app/api/devcase/lifecycle/[id]/approve/route.ts:98 What is conformant: one shared guard is used by both approve paths, a 'none' verdict is a 422 refusal, and the audit runs on the post-edit case. What deviates: the override is recorded as 'probe-audit OVERRIDDEN' under actor 'human' with no name (line 132). Also, the structural audit's third criterion checks `reveals`, not a stated good-versus-naive criterion (devcase-probe-audit.ts:70), so the technique's third pre-ship property is approximated rather than checked.

pairs.registryProposal: probe-discrimination-audit lists three pre-ship properties (options, seam, good-vs-naive criterion), and covert-probe lists 'reveals' as a separate fourth part. Implementations tend to check `reveals` as a proxy for the criterion. The technique could say explicitly that 'reveals' does not satisfy the good-versus-naive criterion.
